home.seoTitle: Free Jungian Cognitive Functions Test | Jung Functions
home.seoDescription: An educational reading of Jung’s eight function-attitudes — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition, each extraverted or introverted. No account.
home.title: Psyche
home.lede: The statements follow Psychological Types, taking each function as it turns toward the outer world or toward the inner impression a thing leaves, and what you get is a sketch of how the psyche orients rather than a verdict on who you are, which is a reading, and therefore incomplete, as all such readings are.

steps.title: Find the leading function
steps.body: The first stretch asks where each function points and what you treat as a reason, and if two leads land together you get a short follow-up before the quiz goes on, so the type is built from the function that actually leads.

steps.title: Fill in the rest of the type
steps.body: The later items score how each function works and include reverse-keyed pairs, so all eight attitudes can be ranked, and the type is built from the lead outward rather than from a four-letter guess made in advance.

steps.title: Read it as a map
steps.body: The closest type is then shown as eight archetypal roles, from the leading function to its most unconscious counterpart, which is a map of the psyche and not a sentence passed upon you.

home.functionsIntro: Jung argued that we all use every function, though we prefer some and struggle with others, and extraversion and introversion here mean where the function points — toward the outer world, or toward the inner impression a thing leaves — not whether you are sociable.

faq.a: In Psychological Types (1921), Jung described four functions — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition — each of which can turn toward the outer world or toward the inner impression a thing leaves, and that gives eight function-attitudes. This quiz then reads your scores through Beebe’s later eight-role model.

faq.q: Is this the official MBTI® test?
faq.a: No. This is a free educational quiz inspired by Jung’s functions. The Myers-Briggs Type Indicator is a separate, trademarked instrument, and we report your eight function scores first, then a likely four-letter type as a reading aid.

faq.q: How long does the quiz take?
faq.a: There are forty-eight statements, six for each function-attitude, including one reverse-keyed item, and the first half looks for the leading function while the rest fills in the type. Most people finish in about eight to ten minutes.
There is no account and no server. Your answers stay in this browser session until you close the tab or start over, and nothing is sent anywhere else.

faq.q: What if two attitudes are equally strong, as Fi and Ti both at 88%?
faq.a: When two functions land that close, the first forty-eight items are not enough to decide, so you get a short follow-up that asks which sentence sounds more like you, and those answers are folded into the percentages to name the lead. If they still split, you choose.

The quiz, the eight scores, and the choice of leading and supporting functions stay free, while the map is a longer reading of why two functions were close, the weaker end of the type, Beebe’s eight roles, and notes on growth, which you can print.

A separate purchase from the map, it reads the other fifteen types against your own functions, not as a ranking of who you should date, but as a picture of where someone else’s leading function already sits in you.

about.seoTitle: About this Jungian functions quiz | Jung Functions
about.seoDescription: How this quiz uses Psychological Types and Beebe’s eight-role model to score the eight function-attitudes.
about.title: About
about.lede: This quiz scores the eight function-attitudes as Jung set them down in Psychological Types (1921), and then reads that profile through Beebe’s later eight-role model, which is a map of the psyche rather than a verdict on who you are.

sections.heading: What Jung measured
paragraphs: Jung distinguished four functions — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition — each able to turn toward the object (extraverted) or toward the subjective factor (introverted). That gives eight function-attitudes. Extraversion here is not sociability; it is whether the function is oriented by the outer object or by the inner impression of the object.

sections.heading: The item bank
paragraphs: There are forty-eight original statements, six for each function-attitude, and the quiz looks for the leading function first, so orientation and criterion items come before process and reverse-keyed ones. If two functions are still close after that stretch, a short follow-up names the lead before the rest of the type is scored. You rate each statement from 1 to 5, and the totals appear as 0–100% bars.

sections.heading: Beebe’s eight roles
paragraphs: Beebe argued that a type is not four functions but eight, each carrying an archetypal charge: Hero, Good Parent, Puer/Puella (Child), Anima/Animus, Opposing Personality, Senex/Witch, Trickster, and Demon/Daimon. The shadow four are the same functions as the ego four, with the opposite attitude. The quiz first scores all eight attitudes, then finds the classical stack whose Beebe pattern best fits that profile, with the leading function weighted first.

sections.heading: How a type is suggested
paragraphs: Each of the sixteen types is scored with the leading function first, so a type whose dominant function is not your strongest score is set aside, while the supporting function is rewarded next, the third moderately, and the inferior only slightly. The model also wants the lead to outrank its opposite-attitude twin. If two functions score close, free results let you pick the lead and the support, and the map opens Child, Anima, and the full eight-role stack.

When two functions land together — Fi and Ti both high, or Ni and Ne — the totals are not enough, so before results the quiz asks a short follow-up: five forced choices between those two, not another set of ratings. Those answers are folded into the percentages, the winner’s bar rises and the other falls, and that is what names the lead. If they still split, you choose.

sections.heading: The full map
paragraphs: The quiz, the eight scores, and a Hero / Parent pick stay free, while the close-score reading, Child and Anima, the full eight-role stack, and the longer chapters sit behind a one-time unlock. Set a Lemon Squeezy or Stripe Payment Link as VITE_DOSSIER_CHECKOUT_URL and put the fulfillment keys in VITE_DOSSIER_UNLOCK_KEYS. After payment, send people to /dossier?key=their-key.

sections.heading: Compatibility add-on
paragraphs: Compatibility is a second, separate unlock. It places the other fifteen types on your Beebe stack (same stack, spine reversed, anima pull, and so on). Use VITE_COMPAT_CHECKOUT_URL and VITE_COMPAT_UNLOCK_KEYS, and send people to /compatibility?key=their-key. A map key will not open compatibility, and a compatibility key will not open the map.

sections.heading: What this is not
paragraphs: This is not psychotherapy, not a medical assessment, and not the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator. MBTI® is a registered trademark of the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator Trust. Jung wrote about functions as living processes. Beebe’s roles describe how those processes can appear in the psyche, not a box you cannot leave.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: There is no account and no database of answers. Optional Cloudflare Web Analytics may count page visits such as /quiz and /results; the answers themselves stay in sessionStorage on your device and are never sent to a server.
